In acute decompensated HF, classifying the patient's hemodynamic profile (warm/cold, wet/dry) guides targeted therapy decisions including diuretics, vasodilators, or inotropes.

Patient has acute decompensated HFmrEF. Early assessment for advanced therapies (ICD, CRT, transplant eligibility) is appropriate as part of comprehensive heart failure management, especially if GDMT is already being optimized.

Beta-blockers are indicated in HFmrEF with EF 41-49%. HR is 80 and BP is stable, making initiation or optimization of beta-blocker therapy appropriate once acute decompensation is stabilizing.

Patient has HFmrEF (EF 41-49%) with acute decompensated heart failure. Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (e.g., spironolactone/eplerenone) are indicated in HFmrEF to reduce mortality and hospitalization when not already on optimal GDMT and renal function/potassium allow.

Patient with acute decompensated HF already started on diuresis. Adding a thiazide-type or carbonic anhydrase inhibitor for combination diuretic therapy may be needed if initial diuretic response is inadequate, given ongoing congestion.

Patient with acute decompensated HFmrEF at 105 minutes should be evaluated for appropriate level of care. If hemodynamically unstable or not responding to initial therapy, ICU-level monitoring is warranted to allow closer titration of diuretics and vasoactive agents.
